title: AI Sales Quotation Generation: Turning Customer Email Inquiries into Customised B2B Quotes
summary: How an AI quotation generator reads customer email inquiries, applies per-customer templates and price lists, and drafts B2B quotes for human approval.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** An AI quotation generator can read a customer's email inquiry, apply that customer's saved template and your price list, and create a draft quote in your accounting system within minutes. It handles the repetitive parts of B2B quoting, such as SLA remarks, maintenance lines, loan unit terms and customer-required declaration lines, while a salesperson refines the draft through chat and approves it before sending. The AI drafts and a human approves, and the accepted quote then flows into the order and invoice without retyping.


For many B2B service and IT firms, the quote is the slowest document in the sales cycle. A customer emails asking for pricing on fifteen notebooks with three-year support. Someone opens the in-house quoting tool, finds the right price, remembers this customer always needs a loan unit clause and a specific declaration line, types it all in, exports a PDF, and replies. If that person is out of the office, the quote waits.


This guide explains how AI quotation generation works for businesses whose quotes are never quite standard. It covers what an AI agent can realistically do with an inbound email, how per-customer template rules keep quotes accurate, why chat-based refinement beats rigid forms, and where humans must stay in control. It is written for teams that currently build quotes by hand in a legacy desktop tool or spreadsheet and want something faster without losing the detail their customers expect.


## What Is an AI Quotation Generator?


An AI quotation generator is software that reads a customer request, identifies the products or services needed, applies your price list and customer-specific rules, and produces a draft quote. In B2B use it acts as a drafting assistant rather than an autonomous seller: the AI prepares the quote, and a person reviews, edits and approves it before it reaches the customer.


The distinction matters. Configure-price-quote (CPQ) tools have existed for years, but most rely on a salesperson filling in structured forms. What changes with AI agents is the starting point. Instead of a blank form, the salesperson starts with a draft built from the customer’s own email, already populated with the right lines, prices and remarks.


Accounting platforms have made this easier because quotes are a native object. Xero, for example, offers[built-in quotes that can be converted to invoices](https://www.xero.com/sg/accounting-software/send-quotes/) , and Microsoft documents a similar flow for[sales quotes in Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/sales-how-make-offers) . An AI agent can create drafts in these systems rather than in a separate tool, so nothing has to be re-entered later.


## Why Are B2B Quotes So Hard to Standardise?


B2B quotes resist standardisation because each customer and project carries its own lines, remarks and terms. A service firm may quote the same notebook to three customers with different support levels, loan unit clauses, payment terms and mandatory declarations. Generic templates cannot capture that variation, so quotes end up assembled by hand.


Consider what a typical IT products and services quote contains beyond the product line itself:


- **Professional services lines** such as installation, imaging, data migration or on-site setup, priced per unit or per hour
- **SLA terms** stating response times, coverage hours and escalation contacts
- **Maintenance lines** for one, two or three years of support, sometimes bundled and sometimes itemised
- **Loan or replacement unit clauses** promising a temporary device during repairs
- **Declaration lines** that particular customers require on every quote, such as tax treatment, warranty conditions or compliance with their supplier code
- **Project-specific pricing** that applies only to a named tender or deployment


The knowledge of which customer needs what usually lives with one or two experienced people. When quotes are built in a heavily customised, on-premise tool that is hard to use remotely, that knowledge bottleneck becomes a speed bottleneck.


The table below shows where time typically goes in a manual quoting process and what changes when an AI agent drafts the quote.


Quoting step Manual process With an AI agent


Read and interpret the inquiry Salesperson reads email and attachments Agent extracts customer, items, quantities and requirements


Find prices Look up price list or past quotes Agent applies current price list and customer discounts


Add standard lines and remarks Recalled from memory or copied from old quotes Agent applies the customer’s saved template


Format the document Typed into legacy tool, exported to PDF Draft created directly in the accounting system


Review and adjust Edit fields one by one Refine by chat instruction, then approve


Convert to order and invoice Retyped in the accounting system Accepted quote converted with lines carried through


## How Does AI Turn a Customer Email into a Quote?


An AI agent turns an email into a quote in four stages: it reads the inquiry and attachments, matches the request to your products and the customer’s template, drafts the quote in your accounting system, and hands it to a person for refinement and approval. Each stage leaves an audit trail so the reviewer can see what the agent inferred.


### 1. Read the inquiry


Inquiries arrive in many shapes: a two-line email, a forwarded tender document, a spreadsheet of required items, or a reply in a long thread. The agent extracts the customer identity, requested items, quantities, delivery location, timing and any special conditions mentioned, such as “must include onsite support” or “quote in line with our framework agreement.”


### 2. Match items and select the template


The agent maps requested items to your product and service master. Customers often describe items loosely, so matching relies on descriptions and past orders, not just exact codes. If a customer sends formal purchase orders with their own part numbers later in the cycle, the same mapping logic applies, as covered in our guide to[customer PO to sales order automation](https://peakflo.co/blog/customer-po-to-sales-order-automation-product-code-mismatch) .


It then selects the template for that customer, and for that project if one exists. The template determines which price list, discounts, standard lines and remarks apply.


### 3. Draft the quote in the accounting system


With items and template resolved, the agent creates a draft quote directly in the accounting platform. With Xero, this uses the standard[Xero quotes API](https://developer.xero.com/documentation/api/accounting/quotes) , which supports draft status, line items, terms and a summary field. Anything the agent cannot resolve, such as an unknown model or a missing quantity, is flagged on the draft rather than guessed.


### 4. Hand off for refinement


The salesperson receives the draft with a short summary of what was extracted and what was assumed. From there, refinement happens in conversation.


## How Do Per-Customer Template Rules Work?


A per-customer template is a saved rule set that tells the AI how to quote a specific customer: which price list or discount applies, which lines to add by default, which remarks and declaration lines are mandatory, and which payment terms and validity period to use. Templates turn tribal knowledge into rules the agent applies consistently.


Templates are usually layered. A default template covers most customers. A customer template overrides parts of it. A project template overrides further for a named deployment or tender. Here is an illustrative example of what that layering looks like.


```text
Template: Customer A (education sector)
Price list:       Standard, minus 8% framework discount
Always add:       Onsite installation (per unit)
3-year next-business-day maintenance
Remarks:          SLA - 4-hour response, Mon-Fri 9am-6pm
Loan unit provided for repairs over 3 working days
Declaration:      “Prices exclude GST. Goods supplied per framework terms.”
Payment terms:    30 days
Quote validity:   14 days
Approval:         Required if discount exceeds 12% or total exceeds limit
Project override: Campus refresh tender
Price list:       Tender price schedule (valid until tender close)
Remarks:          Add delivery schedule by building
```


A few practical guidelines make templates effective:


- **Start with your top customers.** A handful of templates often cover the majority of quote volume.
- **Store remarks as reusable blocks.** SLA wording, loan unit clauses and declarations should be written once and referenced, not retyped.
- **Date project templates.** Tender prices and project terms expire, and the template should stop applying when they do.
- **Let the agent propose template updates.** If a salesperson adds the same line to a customer’s quotes repeatedly, the agent can suggest adding it to the template, subject to approval.


Different template layers carry different rules, as summarised below.


Template layer What it controls Who maintains it When it applies


Default Standard price list, base terms, company remarks Sales operations or finance Every quote unless overridden


Customer Discounts, mandatory lines, SLA and declaration remarks, payment terms Account owner All quotes for that customer


Project Tender or project pricing, delivery details, special clauses Project or bid lead Only quotes tagged to that project, within validity dates


## Why Is Chat Refinement Better Than Editing a Form?


Chat refinement lets a salesperson change a draft quote by giving plain-language instructions, such as “add two spare chargers” or “apply the tender pricing,” instead of editing fields one at a time. It is faster for multi-line changes, works on a phone, and keeps a record of what was changed and why.


This matters most for teams that struggle with legacy tools outside the office. A salesperson visiting a customer can review a draft on a phone and say “change the maintenance to two years and add a loan unit clause,” and the agent updates the draft in the accounting system. No VPN, no desktop client.


Chat refinement works well for:


- Adjusting quantities, adding or removing lines, and switching between support options
- Applying or removing a discount, with the agent checking it against approval thresholds
- Rewording remarks for a specific situation while keeping mandatory declarations intact
- Asking questions about the draft, such as “what margin is this at?” or “when did we last quote this customer?”


It is less suited to brand-new complex solution designs, where a solution architect still needs to define the bill of materials first.


## Where Should Humans Stay in Control?


Humans should approve every quote before it is sent, own the price list and templates, and handle any request the agent flags as ambiguous. The AI drafts, applies rules and catches omissions, but a quote is a commercial commitment. Final judgement on price, terms and customer relationship stays with people.


Responsible AI frameworks make the same point. The[NIST AI Risk Management Framework](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework) emphasises human oversight proportional to risk, and Singapore’s[Model AI Governance Framework](https://www.pdpc.gov.sg/help-and-resources/2020/01/model-ai-governance-framework) describes keeping a human in the loop where decisions have material impact. For quoting, that translates into clear guardrails.


The table below sets out a practical split of responsibilities between the AI agent and the sales team.


Task AI agent Human


Extract request details from email Does it, flags gaps Answers flagged questions


Apply price list and template Does it Maintains price list and templates


Apply discounts within policy Proposes Approves above threshold


Write customer-specific remarks Drafts from templates Edits where context requires


Send quote to customer Never automatically Approves and sends


Convert accepted quote to invoice Prepares Confirms


Approval rules should be explicit. Typical triggers for manager approval include discounts above a set percentage, quotes above a value limit, new customers, and any quote where the agent made an assumption it could not verify.


Data protection also matters, because sales inboxes contain personal data such as contact names and phone numbers. Businesses in Singapore should make sure their use of AI on email complies with the[Personal Data Protection Act](https://www.pdpc.gov.sg/overview-of-pdpa/the-legislation/personal-data-protection-act) , including purpose limitation and appropriate security.


## How Does a Quote Flow into the Order and the Invoice?


Once a customer accepts, the quote should become the order and then the invoice without retyping, so line items, prices and remarks carry through. Linking the three documents prevents billing errors, makes disputes easier to resolve, and gives finance a clear view of what was promised versus what was billed.


In a manual process, the accepted quote is often re-entered into the accounting system as an invoice, sometimes by a different person. That is where the agreed loan unit clause disappears or the framework discount is not applied. Converting the quote directly preserves every line.


Linking also pays off in collections. When a customer disputes an invoice, the team can point to the approved quote and acceptance. For customers that require structured e-invoices, including Singapore government agencies on[InvoiceNow](https://www.imda.gov.sg/how-we-can-help/nationwide-e-invoicing-framework) , clean data from the quote stage makes compliant invoicing simpler. ## Our Verdict: Is AI Quotation Generation Worth It?


### AI quotation generation makes sense if


- Most quote requests arrive by email and are repeat or semi-standard
- Quotes need customer-specific lines, remarks or declarations that people forget
- Your quoting tool is legacy, on-premise or hard to use outside the office
- One or two people hold most of the knowledge about who needs what
- Accepted quotes are retyped as invoices in your accounting system


### Manual quoting may still be fine if


- You send only a handful of highly bespoke quotes each month
- Every quote requires engineering design before pricing
- Your price list changes so often that no reference data stays current


**Our Recommendation:** Start with your most frequent customers and their recurring requests. Build their templates, let the AI draft and keep a human approval step before sending. You will see faster response times and fewer forgotten clauses within weeks, while keeping full control of pricing. To see this with your own price list and templates,[request a demo](https://peakflo.co/request-demo) .


## Conclusion


B2B quoting does not fail because quotes are hard to write. It fails because each customer needs something slightly different, and that knowledge sits in people’s heads and in legacy tools. AI quotation generation changes the starting point: the draft arrives already shaped by the customer’s template, price list and email, and the salesperson spends time refining and approving rather than assembling.


The right model is clear. AI reads, maps and drafts. Humans review, adjust and approve. The accepted quote flows into the order and invoice without retyping. Done this way, quote automation improves speed and consistency without handing pricing decisions to a machine.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is an AI quotation generator?


An AI quotation generator is software that reads a customer’s request, identifies the products or services wanted, applies your price list and customer-specific rules, and produces a draft sales quote. In B2B settings it works best as a drafting assistant: the AI prepares the quote and a person reviews, edits and approves it before it is sent.


### Can AI create a quotation directly from a customer email?


Yes. An AI agent can read an inbound email and its attachments, extract the customer, items, quantities and any special requirements, and create a draft quote in your accounting system. Where the email is ambiguous, such as a missing model number, the agent should flag the gap or ask a clarifying question rather than guess.


### Will AI send quotes to customers without human review?


It should not. A well-designed quotation workflow keeps the AI in drafting mode and requires a person to approve each quote before it is sent. Quotes are commercial commitments, so pricing, terms and customer-specific wording need human sign-off, especially for discounts above a threshold or new customers.


### How do per-customer quotation templates work?


A per-customer template is a saved set of rules for a specific customer: which price list or discount applies, which standard lines to add such as support or delivery, which remarks to include such as SLA terms or a declaration line, and which payment terms and validity period to use. The AI applies the matching template whenever that customer sends an inquiry.


### What are declaration lines on a quotation?


Declaration lines are fixed statements that certain customers require on every quote, for example a statement about product origin, warranty conditions, compliance with their supplier code, or confirmation that prices include or exclude tax. They are easy to forget when quotes are built by hand, which is why storing them in customer templates matters.


### Can I edit an AI-drafted quote by chatting with the agent?


Yes. Chat refinement lets a user give instructions in plain language, such as add a three-year maintenance line, change the quantity to twelve or apply the project discount, and the agent updates the draft. The user then reviews the final version before approving it.


### Does Xero support quotes that can be created automatically?


Yes. Xero has a native quotes feature and exposes quotes through its accounting API, so an integrated system can create draft quotes, update them and later convert accepted quotes into invoices. This keeps the quote, the order and the invoice linked in the same ledger.


### What is the difference between a quotation and a proforma invoice?


A quotation is an offer stating the price and terms at which you are willing to supply goods or services, and the customer may accept or reject it. A proforma invoice is a preliminary bill issued after the terms are broadly agreed, often to support advance payment or import paperwork. Quotes come first in the sales cycle.


### How accurate are AI-generated quotations?


Accuracy depends mainly on the quality of the price list, product master and customer templates the AI draws on. With clean reference data, routine repeat requests can usually be drafted correctly with minor edits. Novel or highly technical requests need more human input, which is why review before sending remains essential.


### Is customer data safe when AI reads sales emails?


It can be, if the platform has appropriate security certifications, access controls and audit trails, and if your use of personal data complies with local law such as Singapore’s PDPA. Ask vendors where data is processed, whether it is used to train models, and how access to the mailbox is scoped.


### How does quote automation connect to invoicing?


Once a customer accepts, the quote becomes the basis for the order and then the invoice, so line items, prices and remarks carry through without retyping. Linking the three documents also makes it easy to check that what was invoiced matches what was quoted, which reduces billing disputes and speeds up collections.
